cards.text: The prophet Isaiah has a message, friend, and it is NOT a gentle one. The Lord has sent a word against Jacob, the people who came from the man God renamed Israel (Gen 32:28), and it has fallen on Israel. All the people will know it: Ephraim, the tribe named for Joseph's son (Gen 41:52), and everyone living in Samaria, the capital of Ephraim (Isa 7:9).

Here's what they say: "The bricks have fallen, but we will rebuild with finished stone; the sycamores have been felled, but we will replace them with cedars." Friend, that's my oven catching fire and me going, 'PERFECT. I always wanted the fancy one.'

cards.question: Isaiah says the people of Ephraim and Samaria talk about rebuilding with ___ in their hearts.

cards.text: Then the LORD raises up the foes of Rezin, king of Aram (Isa 7:1), against him and joins his enemies together. Bigger stones won't fix THIS.

cards.question: Two nations devour Israel with open mouths. Aram comes from the east. Who comes from the west?
After Aram and Philistia devour Israel, Isaiah says the LORD's anger has turned away.

cards.text: Isaiah's words: "Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised." Hang on to that line, friend.

cards.question: After the LORD struck them, what did the people of Israel do?

answers.text: They did not return to Him
They fasted and tore their clothes

cards.text: So the LORD will cut off Israel's head and tail, both palm branch and reed. Top to bottom, friend.

cards.question: Isaiah says the LORD will cut off Israel's head and tail slowly, over many years.
Isaiah explains the picture. The head is the elder and honorable man. Who is the tail?
Isaiah says those who guide this people ___ them.

cards.text: And the ones they mislead are swallowed up. That's the lead driver following his GPS straight into a lake, and every driver behind him going, 'Well, HE looks like he knows.'

cards.question: Isaiah says the Lord takes no pleasure in Israel's young men and has no compassion even on their fatherless and widows. Why?

answers.text: Every one of them is godless and wicked
They refused to leave the land
They bowed down to Aram's gods

cards.text: Every mouth speaks folly, Isaiah says. And there's that line again: "Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised."
Now Isaiah paints a picture. Wickedness burns like a fire that consumes the thorns and briers and kindles the forest thickets, rolling upward in billows of smoke.

cards.question: Isaiah says the land is scorched by the ___ of the LORD of Hosts.

cards.text: The people are fuel for the fire, and no man even spares his brother. His OWN brother, friend. Let that sit for a second.

cards.question: The people carve out what's on the right and eat what's on the left. Isaiah says they end up satisfied.

cards.text: Still hungry, still not satisfied, and it gets darker. Each one devours the flesh of his own offspring.

cards.question: Isaiah names two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim, named for Joseph's two sons (Gen 41:51-52). They devour each other. Then who do they turn against together?

cards.text: Judah, another of the tribes of Israel (Gen 49:8, 28). And for the THIRD time: "Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised."

Now Isaiah turns to the people who write the rules, and he opens with WOE: woe to those who make unjust laws and issue oppressive decrees. Friend, these folks don't just bend the rules. They WRITE the bent ones.

cards.question: Those unjust laws and decrees are made to deprive the ___ of fair treatment.
Isaiah says these lawmakers make widows their prey and orphans their plunder.

cards.text: Then come the hard questions: "What will you do on the day of reckoning when devastation comes from afar?" There's no snooze button on THAT alarm.

cards.question: The questions for those unjust lawmakers keep coming: "To whom will you flee for help? Where will you leave your wealth?" What do these questions point to?

answers.text: Their wealth will buy them time

cards.question: When devastation comes from afar, Isaiah says only two things remain for those lawmakers. What are they?

cards.text: One last time: "Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised." That's FOUR times, friend, and I spent years counting dust in a junk drawer, so trust me, I counted.

findings.problem: Card 9 omits the timing from Isaiah 9:14, and nothing earlier indicates whether the cutting off is slow or swift. The baker can only coin-flip between True and False; moreover, no later card supplies the actual detail that it happens in a single day.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the statement about the people being fuel and not sparing a brother, then 'His OWN brother, friend.' and then 'Let that sit for a second.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: No earlier card discusses hunger, eating or satisfaction. The question itself introduces the carving and eating on the right and left, but gives the baker no contextual basis for deciding whether the people end up satisfied, making this another luck-only True or False pick.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
